# Amazon Hardware for AI

Amazon EC2, which means Elastic Compute Cloud, is one of the most popular offerings from AWS. 

- This is where you **get your servers** as part of an <u>infrastructure as a service</u>  **(IAAS)** model. 

While EC2 is not as central from an AI perspective because we often use managed AWS services, it's still important to have an overview. 

- EC2 is fundamentally about **renting virtual machines or servers in the cloud**, and knowing how it works is key to understanding the cloud itself.

### **Amazon EC2 Overview**                                      <img title="" src="https://miro.medium.com/v2/resize:fit:792/1*UfkVdTaCy-ArRy3QgoZcbA.png" alt="AWS EC2. A short note on what to know about EC2 | by Michael ..." width="50">

When you have your virtual server, you can configure many aspects of it. You are pretty much creating a virtual computer on which you define what you want on it and how powerful you want it to be.

- You can <u>attach disk space</u> to these servers using **EBS drives**.

- You can <u>distribute traffic</u> to your Amazon EC2 instances through **load balancers (ELB)**.

- You can scale the service automatically using **auto-scaling groups (ASG)**.

You can also define the following for your virtual server:

1. **Operating System:** Choose from Linux, Windows, or Mac OS.

2. **Compute & Memory:** Define how much compute (CPU cores) and Random Access Memory (RAM) you want.

3. **Storage Space:** Specify how much storage you need, which can be <span style="color:blue;font-weight:bold;">network-attached</span> or <span style="color:blue;font-weight:bold;">hardware-based</span>.

4. **Network & IP:** Define <u>how fast you want the network to be</u> and if you want a <u>public IP</u>.

5. **Firewall Rules:** If you are <u>exposing the server</u>, you can set firewall rules called **security groups**.

6. **Launch Configuration:** To configure your virtual server at launch, you can use **<u>EC2 User Data</u>**.

### **Amazon EC2 for Artificial Intelligence (AI)**

When you create an Amazon EC2 instance, you must select an **instance type**. Some EC2 instances are based on GPUs or specialized machine learning chips, making them desirable from an AI perspective.

**1. GPU-Based Instances**

- A **GPU** (Graphical Processing Unit) is a very good processor that allows you to perform machine learning.

- EC2 families like the **P family** (P3, P4, P5) and the **G family** (G3, G6) have powerful GPUs and are great for machine learning.

**2. AWS Trainium**

- These are **<u>machine learning chips</u>** used to perform **<u>deep learning on big models</u>** with over **100 billion parameters**.

- You would use these servers to <u>train models</u> if, for example, you don't want to use SageMaker.
  
  ![Amazon EC2 Trn1 Instances for High ...](data:image/jpeg;base64,)

- The **Trn1** instance, for example, will have <u>16 Trainium accelerators</u> and can provide a **50% cost reduction** for training.

**AWS Inferentia**

- This is a <u>**machine learning chip**</u> built by AWS for <u>running inference at very high performance and low cost</u>. You can use these servers to **serve the models**.
  
  ![Amazon EC2 Inf2 Instances for Low-Cost, High-Performance Generative AI  Inference are Now Generally Available | AWS News Blog](https://d2908q01vomqb2.cloudfront.net/da4b9237bacccdf19c0760cab7aec4a8359010b0/2023/02/16/Site-Merch_Full-Build_Amazon-EC2-Inf2_Blog.png)

- **Inf1** or **Inf2** instances are powered by **AWS Inferentia**.

- Using these chips can result in up to **4 times the throughput** of a normal GPU-based instance and up to a **70% cost reduction**.

**Environmental Footprint**

- Something that can appear in the exam is that the **Trainium** and **Inferentia** instances have the <mark>lowest environmental footprint</mark> because they are the most efficient.

### **Exam Summary**

From an exam perspective, remember that EC2 instances are virtual servers and they can be of different types. You have **GPU-based types** and also the ones based on **AWS Trainium** and **AWS Inferentia**.





> Important Note: 
> 
> 1. AWS Trainium is ML chip for training of DL models
> 
> 2. AWS Inferentia is ML chip for **serving the model**.
